_comment: Optional downloadable add-ons. Kept separate from manifest.json because CI
regenerates that file from pack fragments on every pack release and would
discard anything else in it, and because add-ons ship on their own cadence.
The add-on is platform-neutral: it is model weights, not executables, so one
artifact serves Windows, macOS and Linux. It installs into the Docling pack's
own models directory because Docling resolves every model against a single
artifacts_path that the pack worker pins there.
url, sha256, size_bytes, uncompressed_size_bytes and sha256_files are written
by .github/workflows/build-addon.yml, which derives the URL from the release
tag and commits the result back. Do not edit them by hand: this file used to
be filled in from a printed blob, which is how it came to hold a placeholder
URL that AddonManager.get_status reported as installable.
Both url and sha256 empty is the 'unreleased' state, and is valid: the add-on
reports available=false, install is refused, and the enrichment toggles stay
disabled. Any other incomplete combination is a defect and fails
scripts/verify_addon_catalogue.py in CI.
min_pack_version is 6.0.0 because the installer confirms a new install with
the worker's 'capabilities' RPC, which pack v5's worker does not implement,
and because the worker refuses enrichment outright when the model is absent
instead of quietly converting without it. worker.py is hashed into the pack
manifest and the launcher rejects a modified copy, so an older pack cannot
be given either behaviour.

code_enrichment.title: Code & Formula Recognition
code_enrichment.description: Transcribes code blocks and mathematical formulas from page images using Docling's recognition model, and labels the programming language of each code block.
